title: Active learning improves a cell-free carbon-fixation cycle
summary: An ensemble learned from experimental feedback to select compositions for an engineered carbon-fixation cycle. Laboratory measurements supported improved glycolate production compared with the study's reference cycle. This is an in-vitro pathway result, not carbon capture by living organisms or a demonstrated industrial process. Other applications in the same paper are not additional catalog entries.
organization: Max Planck Institute for Terrestrial Microbiology

evidence.tested: Selected pathway compositions received biochemical measurements.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication, in-vivo function and scale-up remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: METIS XGBoost active learning supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.
